items.stem:
A metal ‘M’ on reacting with dilute acid liberates a gas ‘G’. The same metal also liberates gas ‘G’ when it reacts with a base.
(i) Write the name of gas ‘G’.
(ii) How will you test the presence of this gas?
(iii) Write chemical equations for the reactions of the metal with (1) an acid and (2) a base.
items.answer:
(i) Hydrogen gas.
(ii) On bringing a burning match stick near the mouth of the test tube, a pop sound occurs.
(iii) Reaction with acid: Zn(s) + 2HCl(aq) → ZnCl₂(aq) + H₂(g)
Reaction with base: 2NaOH(aq) + Zn(s) → Na₂ZnO₂(aq) + H₂(g)

items.stem:
A shining metal M on burning gives a dazzling white flame and changes to a white powder N.
(a) Identify M and N.
(b) Represent the above reaction in the form of a balanced chemical equation.
(c) Does M undergo oxidation or reduction in this reaction? Justify.
items.answer:
(a) M – Magnesium, N – Magnesium oxide.
(b) 2Mg(s) + O₂(g) → 2MgO(s)
     magnesium + oxygen → magnesium oxide
(c) M undergoes oxidation, because oxygen is added to the metal M and the metal oxide is formed. When a piece of the shining metal M is burnt in air, a white powder of metal oxide is formed. The shining metal is a magnesium ribbon, which burns with a dazzling white flame, and the white powder formed is magnesium oxide.

items.stem: Write some physical properties of metals.
items.answer:
(i) All metals except mercury are solid at room temperature.
(ii) Metals possess metallic lustre.
(iii) They are malleable and ductile.
(iv) They are good conductors of heat and electricity.
(v) They (except sodium) are sonorous and have high density.
(vi) They are generally hard, except sodium and potassium.
(vii) Metals have high boiling and melting points, except sodium and potassium.

items.stem: What happens when metal oxides are dissolved in water? Write the chemical reaction.
items.answer:
Most of the metal oxides are insoluble in water. Some metal oxides, like sodium oxide and potassium oxide, dissolve in water to form an alkali.
Na₂O + H₂O → 2NaOH
(Sodium oxide, a metal oxide) → (Sodium hydroxide, an alkali)
K₂O + H₂O → 2KOH
(Potassium oxide, a metal oxide) → (Potassium hydroxide, an alkali)

items.stem:
(a) What is meant by reactivity series of metals?
(b) Why are metals not equally reactive? Arrange the following metals in decreasing order of their reactivity: Fe, Ag, Na, Cu, Al.
items.answer:
(a) The arrangement of metals in order of decreasing reactivity is called the reactivity series of metals.
(b) All metals are not equally reactive. The basis of reactivity is the tendency of a metal to lose electrons. Metals which can lose electrons more easily to form positive ions are more reactive; less reactive metals do not lose electrons easily.
Decreasing order of reactivity: Na > Al > Fe > Cu > Ag

items.stem: Write an experiment to show that copper does not react with dilute HCl.
items.answer: Take small pieces of magnesium, zinc, aluminium, iron and copper. Clean their surfaces by rubbing with sand paper. Place these metals in separate test tubes. Add about 10 mL of dilute hydrochloric acid to each of these test tubes. Observe carefully the rate of formation of bubbles. We will find that the rate of formation of bubbles is fastest in the case of magnesium. It decreases in the order Mg > Al > Zn > Fe. In the case of copper, no bubbles are evolved. This shows that copper does not react with dilute HCl and H₂SO₄.
items.ocr: Dropped letters restored: 'we will ind' → 'find', 'rate of ormation' → 'formation'.

items.stem: A copper plate was dipped into a solution of AgNO₃. After some time, a black layer was deposited on the copper plate. State the reason for it. Write the chemical equation of the reaction involved.
items.answer:
A black layer was deposited on the copper plate because copper, being more reactive than silver, displaces silver from silver nitrate and forms copper nitrate.
2AgNO₃ (silver nitrate) + Cu → Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2Ag

items.stem:
(a) Arrange the metals Zn, Mg, Al, Cu and Fe in decreasing order of reactivity.
(b) What would you observe when you put
(i) some zinc pieces into blue copper sulphate solution?
(ii) some copper pieces into green ferrous sulphate solution?
(c) Name a metal which combines with hydrogen gas. Name the compound formed.
items.answer:
(a) Decreasing order of reactivity: Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Cu
(b) (i) Zinc, being more reactive than copper, displaces copper from copper sulphate. The blue colour of the copper sulphate solution fades and a colourless solution is obtained. Reddish brown particles of copper settle at the bottom of the container.
Zn + CuSO₄ (blue) → ZnSO₄ + Cu
(ii) No change in the colour of the solution, as copper is less reactive than iron.
(c) Sodium combines with hydrogen gas. The compound formed is sodium hydride.
2Na + H₂ → 2NaH (sodium hydride)

items.stem:
(i) Which metals can displace hydrogen?
(ii) Which metals cannot displace hydrogen?
items.answer:
(i) Metals placed above hydrogen in the reactivity series are more reactive than hydrogen and can displace hydrogen from its compounds like acids, e.g., sodium, calcium, etc.
(ii) Metals placed below hydrogen in the reactivity series are less reactive than hydrogen and cannot displace hydrogen from its compounds like acids, e.g., silver, gold, etc.

items.stem: State the reason for the following behaviour of zinc metal: On placing a piece of zinc metal in a solution of mercuric chloride, it acquires a shining silvery surface, but when it is placed in a solution of magnesium sulphate, no change is observed.
items.answer:
On placing a piece of zinc metal in a solution of mercuric chloride, it acquires a shining silvery surface because zinc, being more reactive than mercury, displaces mercury from mercuric chloride and forms zinc chloride.
Zn + HgCl₂ → ZnCl₂ + Hg
When zinc is placed in magnesium sulphate solution, no reaction takes place because zinc is less reactive than magnesium and hence cannot displace magnesium from magnesium sulphate.

items.stem: How does the activity series of metals help us in predicting the relative reactivity of metals?
items.answer:
(i) In the reactivity series, the most reactive metal is placed at the top. It does not occur in the free state and is more electropositive.
(ii) The least reactive metal is placed at the bottom. It generally occurs in the free state and is less electropositive.
(iii) A metal displaces any of the metals below it in the reactivity series from their solutions.
(iv) Metals above hydrogen in the reactivity series displace hydrogen from acids.
items.ocr: 'A metal displaces anyel the metals below it' → 'any of the metals below it'.

items.stem:
(a) Why are metals generally not found in their free state?
(b) If a strip of aluminium with a scratched clean surface is dipped into an aqueous solution of copper sulphate for a little time, the surface of the strip becomes brownish. What is the reason for this? Write the balanced chemical equation for the reaction.
items.answer:
(a) Metals are reactive atoms as they are highly electropositive. They readily react with other atoms during their formation in the earth and become compounds.
(b) A displacement reaction takes place, as aluminium is more reactive than copper. The copper displaced sticks on the aluminium strip, making it brownish.
2Al(s) + 3CuSO₄(aq) → Al₂(SO₄)₃(aq) + 3Cu(s)

items.stem:
(a) Using a simple experiment, how can you prove that magnesium is placed above zinc in the reactivity series?
(b) Why can copper metal not liberate hydrogen when reacting with dil. HCl?
items.answer:
(a) Dip a magnesium rod in ZnSO₄ solution, or heat magnesium powder with zinc oxide powder. Magnesium displaces zinc from its compound.
Mg(s) + ZnSO₄(aq) → MgSO₄(aq) + Zn(s)
or Mg(s) + ZnO(s) → MgO(s) + Zn(s)
This shows that magnesium is placed above zinc in the reactivity series.
(b) Copper is less reactive and is placed below hydrogen in the reactivity series of metals. Hence it does not react with dil. HCl.

items.stem:
(a) An element X on reacting with oxygen forms an oxide X₂O. The oxide dissolves in water and turns blue litmus red. Predict the nature of the element, whether metal or non-metal.
(b) A solution of copper sulphate was kept in an iron pot. After a few days, the pot developed some holes in it. How will you account for this?
items.answer:
(a) Element X is a non-metal.
(b) Iron lies above copper in the activity series. Therefore a chemical reaction took place between the iron pot and the copper sulphate solution, i.e., iron displaced copper from the copper sulphate solution.
Fe(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → Cu(s) + FeSO₄(aq)

items.stem: Which method can be used in place of reduction by carbon?
items.answer: Besides using carbon (coke) to reduce metal oxides to metals, displacement reactions can also be used. The highly reactive metals such as sodium, calcium, aluminium, etc., are used as reducing agents because they can displace metals of lower reactivity from their compounds.

items.stem: Describe the calcination of zinc ore.
items.answer:
Calcination of a zinc ore such as ZnCO₃ is carried out by heating it strongly in a limited supply of air:
ZnCO₃(s) —Heat→ ZnO(s) + CO₂(g)
Zinc oxide is then reduced to zinc metal by using a suitable reducing agent such as carbon.
ZnO(s) + C(s) → Zn(s) + CO(g)

items.stem: What happens when molten NaCl is electrolysed?
items.answer:
Sodium metal is deposited at the cathode (the negatively charged electrode), whereas chlorine is liberated at the anode (the positively charged electrode). The reactions are:
At cathode: Na⁺ + e⁻ → Na
At anode: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻

items.stem: Write the balanced chemical equation for the chemical reaction between manganese dioxide and aluminium powder. What happens if manganese powder is heated with aluminium oxide?
items.answer:
3MnO₂(s) + 4Al(s) → 3Mn(s) + 2Al₂O₃(s) + Heat
If manganese powder is heated with aluminium oxide, no reaction takes place, because Mn is less reactive than Al and hence no displacement occurs.

items.stem:
Give reasons for the following:
(i) Ionic compounds usually have high melting and boiling points.
(ii) Metals are good conductors of electricity whereas non-metals are not.
items.answer:
(i) Because a considerable amount of energy is required to break the strong inter-ionic attraction.
(ii) Metals have free electrons, while non-metals (insulators) do not have any free electrons.

items.stem: The atomic number of magnesium is 12 and that of chlorine is 17. Show the formation of magnesium chloride by the transfer of electrons.
items.answer:
Magnesium (2, 8, 2) loses its two valence electrons to attain the stable configuration of neon and becomes Mg²⁺. Each chlorine atom (2, 8, 7) accepts one of these electrons to complete its octet and becomes Cl⁻. Two chloride ions are needed for each magnesium ion.
Mg + 2Cl → [Mg]²⁺ + 2[Cl]⁻ → MgCl₂
The oppositely charged ions are held together by strong electrostatic force, forming the ionic compound magnesium chloride.

items.stem: Ionic compounds conduct electricity only in the molten state, not in the solid state. Why?
items.answer: Ionic compounds conduct electricity only in the molten state because the electrostatic forces of attraction between the oppositely charged ions are overcome due to heat, so the ions become free to move. In the solid state, movement of ions is not possible due to their rigid structure.

items.stem: How does rusting take place? Write the conditions necessary for rusting to take place.
items.answer:
(i) Rusting: It is an oxidation process in which iron metal is slowly oxidised by the action of air in the presence of moisture. Rust is a mixture of ferric oxide and ferric hydroxide. It is a brown, flaky substance.
(ii) Conditions necessary for rusting:
(a) Presence of air (or oxygen).
(b) Presence of moisture.

items.stem: Describe ways to prevent rusting.
items.answer:
The rusting of iron can be prevented by the following methods:
(a) By coating the metal surface with a thin layer of paint, varnish or grease.
(b) By coating iron with a thin layer of another metal which is more reactive than iron, e.g., by galvanisation. Galvanisation is the process of covering iron with zinc.
(c) It can also be prevented by the use of anti-rust solutions.

(ii) Aluminium is a very reactive metal, so it can be extracted only by electrolysis.
(iii) Gold is a very unreactive element, so it is found in the native state.

(b) Why has sodium chloride a high melting point?

items.stem: What is meant by refining of metals? Describe the electrolytic refining of copper with a neat labelled diagram.
items.answer:
In the electrolytic refining process, the impure metal is made the anode and a thin strip of pure metal is made the cathode. A solution of the metal salt is used as the electrolyte. On passing current through the electrolyte, the metal from the impure anode dissolves into the electrolyte, and an equivalent amount of pure metal from the electrolyte is deposited on the cathode. The soluble impurities go into the solution, whereas the insoluble impurities settle down at the bottom of the anode and are known as anode mud.
At anode: Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻
At cathode: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu

Printed text 'the pure metal from the anode dissolves' read as the impure-anode metal dissolving.

items.stem:
(a) Show the formation of Na₂O by the transfer of electrons between the combining atoms.
(b) Why are ionic compounds usually hard?
(c) How is it that ionic compounds in the solid state do not conduct electricity, and they do so when in the molten state?
items.answer:
(a) Sodium has one electron in its outermost shell and oxygen has six electrons in its outermost shell. To complete their octets, two sodium atoms each lose one electron and oxygen accepts both, giving [Na⁺]₂[O²⁻], i.e., Na₂O.
(b) Ionic compounds are usually hard because of the strong electrostatic forces of attraction between the oppositely charged ions.
(c) Ionic compounds in the solid state do not conduct electricity because these compounds do not dissociate to produce free ions; but in the molten state ionic compounds dissociate to produce free ions and hence they conduct electricity.

items.stem:
State which of the following reactions will take place or not, and why.
(i) Zn(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → ZnSO₄(aq) + Cu(s)
(ii) Fe(s) + ZnSO₄(aq) → FeSO₄(aq) + Zn(s)
(iii) Zn(s) + FeSO₄(aq) → ZnSO₄(aq) + Fe(s)
items.answer:
(i) Zn(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → ZnSO₄(aq) + Cu(s)
This reaction will take place, as zinc is more reactive than copper and can therefore displace copper from its aqueous solution.
(ii) Fe(s) + ZnSO₄(aq) → FeSO₄(aq) + Zn(s)
This reaction will not take place, since iron is less reactive than zinc and therefore cannot displace it.
(iii) Zn(s) + FeSO₄(aq) → ZnSO₄(aq) + Fe(s)
This reaction will take place, as zinc is more reactive than iron and can therefore displace iron from its aqueous solution.

items.stem:
(a) Show the formation of Na₂O by the transfer of electrons between the combining atoms.
(b) Why are ionic compounds usually hard?
(c) How is it that ionic compounds in the solid state do not conduct electricity, and they do so when in the molten state?
items.answer:
(a) Formation of Na₂O: each of two sodium atoms loses one electron (Na → Na⁺ + e⁻) and the oxygen atom accepts both electrons (O + 2e⁻ → O²⁻), giving [Na⁺]₂[O²⁻], i.e., Na₂O.
(b) It is because of the strong force of attraction between the positive and negative ions.
(c) Ionic compounds in the solid state do not conduct electricity because movement of ions in the solid is not possible due to their rigid structure. But ionic compounds conduct electricity in the molten state: in the molten state the electrostatic forces of attraction between the oppositely charged ions are overcome due to heat, so the ions move freely and conduct electricity.

items.stem: What kind of impurities are generally found in ores? What name is given to such impurities, and state the basis of removing the impurities from the ore.
items.answer: Ores mined from the earth are usually contaminated with large amounts of impurities such as soil, sand, etc. These impurities are called gangue. The processes used for removing the gangue from the ore are based on the differences between the physical or chemical properties of the gangue and the ore.
items.ocr: 'Ores mixed from the earth' read as 'Ores mined from the earth'.

items.stem:
(a) A non-metal X exists in two different forms Y and Z. Y is the hardest natural substance, whereas Z is a good conductor of electricity. Identify X, Y and Z.
(b) An element X on reaction with oxygen forms an oxide XO₂. The oxide, when dissolved in water, turns blue litmus red. State whether element X is a metal or a non-metal.
(c) Name the metal which is alloyed with copper to make bronze.
items.answer:
(a) X is carbon. Y and Z are allotropes of carbon. Y (hardest natural substance) is diamond; Z (good conductor of electricity) is graphite.
(b) X is a non-metal.
X + O₂ → XO₂, e.g., C + O₂ → CO₂, and the oxide turns blue litmus red.
(c) Tin.
